pairs.subject: optional-dependency-degradation
pairs.evidence: features/lawwatch/getRadarData.ts:40 When only one half of the radar loads (for example no store, so getLawData returns null while getCollisionData still reads its payload files), the missing half becomes an empty array, so RadarData reports a definite 0 for that kind and the page and both feeds publish a complete-looking ledger with no marker that the half could not be looked at.

techniques.evidence: features/lawwatch/getRadarData.ts:40 An unavailable source is rounded to an empty collection; RadarData has no partial or source-unavailable field, RadarLedger renders '0 příznaků', and the feeds refuse (503) only when BOTH halves are null. Same family: buildDependencyView asNum turns a missing payload count into a rendered 0. The both-null path is honest: 503 with no-store, and DependencyRadar's null state says it is not a finding of no dependencies.

features/lawwatch/buildDependencyView.ts:231 The caller-supplied GateFn refuses by returning null; a hit refused on both fields is withheld and counted, never rendered through a default. A throw from the gate propagates to the loader's outer catch, which reports it and returns null.

features/lawwatch/getDependencyData.ts:43 The input is a compile-time constant path to a checked-in artifact; a grep of features/lawwatch found no process.env read, so no operator value exists to branch on.

features/lawwatch/getDependencyData.ts:44 No configuration reader or identifier filter exists here. A corrupt census file does take the same triage-excerpt fallback as an absent one, but it is a data artifact, not operator configuration, and the catch reports it.
features/lawwatch/radarFeedCodecs.ts:23 The context introduces no configuration variable; the only deployment-shaped value, the feed origin, is injected by the caller.
features/lawwatch/getRadarData.ts:5 No client is constructed in this context; the radar composes existing loaders, which own the store access.
features/lawwatch/getDependencyData.ts:129 No credential or storage-tier choice exists; the check tests the same local file the read then opens, and nothing here writes.
features/lawwatch/getDependencyData.ts:35 The fallback reads local checked-in files and never writes, so it has no grants to lose.
features/lawwatch/getDependencyData.ts:136 The census fallback covers a missing or unreadable artifact, not a platform gap expected to close on a schedule, so no reaper is owed.

pairs.registryProposal: capability-honest-refusal states partial-outcome rules mostly for writes and connector quantities; it could name the composite read explicitly, where a view merges N sources and one is unavailable, requiring the output to carry per-source availability instead of merging an empty half. The subject also has no wording for checked-in data artifacts as the optional dependency, where the absent-versus-malformed asymmetry plausibly applies but boot-time refusal does not obviously fit.
